verdict_summary: needs-fix, not pass. Blocking: the reviewed product wp-331-01 is unreachable, so claim-level fidelity cannot be audited. Substantive: even judged on the source alone, four major defects must be fixed before any knowledge object from this report is reusable — (F3) the Hertz comparison runs at delta/R = 0.5, far outside Hertzias validity, (F4) the causal attribution 'lattice cannot reproduce Hertz' is confounded by dynamic loading and an untested E_dem calibration, (F5) the only PASS (beam 0.0125%) and the claimed O(1/n^2) order have no reference value or mesh series, (F6) a 58.6% energy drift disqualifies the trajectory that produced the reported exponent/stiffness. The report's own honest-FAIL discipline is good and its three FAIL verdicts are arithmetic-consistent; they are not the defect.

derived_metrics.indent_over_R_note: Hertz small-strain validity needs delta/R << 1; the reported final indentation reaches delta/R =0.50

findings.statement: Upstream package wp-331-01 has no retrievable product, so the claim-level fidelity of the extraction (03 output) cannot be audited; this package can therefore not be approved, only refused/returned.
findings.analysis: Channels checked: (a) platform report listing — 100 most recent records scanned client-side for the tag kf-wp:wp-331-01, zero hits; the reports endpoint honours neither ?tag= nor ?offset= (both return the newest 50-100 rows), so an exhaustive scan is impossible from here; (b) no work-package endpoint (/tensor/work-packages, /tensor/packages -> HTTP 404); (c) psql: 'permission denied for table tensor_reports'; (d) worktree artifacts: no file matching wp-331-* outside this package. Therefore the review is executed against the only reachable authoritative evidence, the source markdown, and every 03-style claim below is judged for whether the source can support it.
findings.remediation: Attach the wp-331-01 product (claims/evidence/provenance) to the package and re-run this review; acceptance item upstream_packages_completed stays FALSE until then.

findings.statement: The title advertises a 'DEM-FEM Coupling Interface Schema', but the body declares TensorFEM unavailable: no coupling is executed, and no schema artifact, path or validator output is given.

evidence.quote: **Honest-FAIL**: TensorFEM unavailable; DEM lattice ≠ continuum half-space

findings.analysis: Two separate assertions are collapsed into one: 'a schema exists' and 'it validates'. The report supplies neither the schema file, its $id/version, nor the validator command and exit status, so 'validates against jsonschema' is unfalsifiable from the text. Any 03 claim asserting a validated DEM-FEM interface schema must be status=unresolved, not supported; a claim naming DEM-FEM *coupling* (as opposed to interface-schema authoring) as demonstrated is scope drift.
findings.remediation: Either attach the schema file + validator transcript (path, command, exit code, jsonschema version) or restate the delivery as 'interface schema draft, unvalidated; FEM side not available'.

findings.statement: The Hertz comparison is run over a load range that violates Hertz's own small-strain condition, so the 1.4108 exponent is not a clean measure of discretisation error and the ±0.05 acceptance band is mis-specified for this range.

evidence.quote: **Geometry**: DEM3D bonded-sphere assembly (4×3×4 grid) with spherical indenter (R=0.1m)

findings.analysis: max_indent / R = 0.05 / 0.1 = 0.5, i.e. delta/R = 0.5 at the end of the stroke. Hertz (F proportional to delta^1.5) assumes delta/R << 1 (single-digit-percent strains); at delta/R = 0.5 both the geometric linearisation and the half-space assumption fail, and the fitted exponent drifts below 1.5 for reasons that have nothing to do with the lattice. The honest FAIL verdict itself is therefore not evidence that the DEM discretisation is inadequate.
findings.remediation: Restrict the fit window to small strain (e.g. delta/R <= 0.05-0.1), report the fitted exponent per window, and only then compare against 1.5 +/- 0.05; alternatively declare the finite-strain regime and compare against a finite-deformation contact solution instead of Hertz.

findings.statement: 'DEM discrete lattice cannot reproduce continuum Hertz contact' is stated as the cause of the 44.1% stiffness error, but the setup confounds at least four candidate causes that the report never separates.

evidence.quote: - DEM discrete lattice cannot reproduce continuum Hertz contact

findings.analysis: Candidate causes, none excluded by the reported evidence: (i) the ad-hoc calibration E_dem ~ k_bond/(2r) is not derived and its agreement with the continuum E* of the assembly is never tested; (ii) tool_speed = 5 m/s means the indentation is dynamic — inertial/drag forces superpose on the static contact law, and no ramp/relaxation or quasi-static protocol is documented; (iii) the assembly is 4x3x4 spheres, i.e. the compliant half-space is a few sphere diameters thick, so a stiff far boundary is plausible; (iv) the lattice anisotropy of a bonded-sphere packing. A single-run FAIL cannot attribute the error to (iv) alone, which is what the note asserts.
findings.remediation: Add a discriminating experiment per candidate: (a) calibrate E_dem against a two-sphere/bulk-modulus test, (b) load at << 5 m/s or with energy-damped relaxation, (c) grow the assembly depth and show convergence of the contact stiffness. Then the residual can be attributed to the lattice.

findings.statement: The only PASS item (beam stiffness 0.0125%) and the claimed second-order convergence are not reproducible from the report: no reference value, no beam data, no mesh series.

evidence.quote: - Beam fallback: FD Euler-Bernoulli with simply-supported BCs

findings.analysis: A relative error needs a reference. The report gives neither the analytic simply-supported deflection used as reference, nor L, EI, P, nor the grid resolution, so 0.0125% cannot be recomputed or checked for a units/normalisation mistake (a factor-100 slip would look like a superb PASS). The 'second-order convergence' claim likewise rests on a single number (8.4% 'Mesh conv', metric undefined) rather than a mesh sequence with a fitted slope, so it is a hypothesis, not a measurement.
findings.remediation: Report the numeric reference (delta_ref = 5wL^4/384EI or equivalent), the case constants, and at least three mesh levels n = 40/80/160 with errors and the fitted log-log slope (expected -2).

findings.statement: An energy drift of 58.6% against a ≤1% target invalidates the DEM trajectory from which the exponent and stiffness are extracted; the defective trajectory cannot support any contact-law conclusion.
findings.analysis: 58.6% vs 1.0% is a 58.6x overshoot. Neither the integrator, the timestep, the damping model nor the energy definition ('drift' relative to initial PE?) is stated, so the audit cannot even distinguish a genuine integration error from a wrong energy accounting. Any knowledge object that carries the DEM exponent/stiffness numbers without this defect attached is over-claiming.
findings.remediation: State integrator and dt, report total (kinetic+potential+contact) energy conservation for a free-flight and a resting-contact control case, and re-run the indentation only after drift < 1%.

findings.statement: The FAIL line conflates a relative percentage with an absolute tolerance: 1.4108 vs 1.5 is a 0.0892 absolute shortfall, 1.78x the stated +-0.05 band, not '5.9% outside a 5% band' as the wording suggests.
findings.analysis: Computed: |1.4108 - 1.5| = 0.0892 (relative 5.9467%), overshoot = 1.784x the 0.05 tolerance. The verdict FAIL is correct and unaffected; only the audit trail is imprecise.
findings.remediation: State the absolute deviation (0.0892) alongside the percentage.

findings.statement: The report carries no run identity: no commit, no input deck path, no seed, no sphere radius / packing fraction / timestep, no figure paths.

evidence.quote: See attached: Hertz F-δ curve + beam deflection comparison

findings.analysis: Record carries figures = 1; the text points to 'attached' curves without file names, so a reviewer cannot bind the plotted quantity to the table numbers. The geometry line gives the grid (4x3x4) and the indenter radius but not the sphere radius r that the E_dem ~ k_bond/(2r) calibration needs — the calibration therefore cannot be recomputed at all.
findings.remediation: Add a run-identity block: repo+commit, input deck path, sphere radius, packing fraction, dt, seed, figure file names.

claim_judgements.text: Hertz exponent 1.4108 vs target 1.5 +- 0.05 is a FAIL.
claim_judgements.reasoning: Arithmetic confirms the FAIL: |1.4108-1.5| = 0.0892 > 0.05. The claim is faithful to the source and correctly signed; only its phrasing is imprecise (F7). What it may NOT be used to support is the causal reading 'lattice cannot do Hertz' (F3, F4).

claim_judgements.text: Hertz stiffness error 44.1% vs target <=3% is a FAIL.
claim_judgements.reasoning: The FAIL verdict is arithmetic-consistent (44.1/3 = 14.7x the budget), but the 44.1% itself is not recomputable: E* needs Poisson's ratio and E_dem needs the sphere radius r, neither is stated. A knowledge object must carry the number as 'as-reported, base quantities missing', not as a verified material property of the lattice.

claim_judgements.text: Beam FD (n=80) stiffness error 0.0125% vs <=3% is a PASS.
claim_judgements.reasoning: No reference deflection, beam constants or normalisation convention appears in the report, so the PASS is unfalsifiable (F5). It must not be promoted to a reusable 'FD Euler-Bernoulli is validated to 1e-4' knowledge claim.

claim_judgements.text: Energy drift 58.6% vs <=1% target is a FAIL.
claim_judgements.reasoning: 1% target, 58.6% measured: 58.6x over budget. Verdict supported and, per F6, it is the most consequential number in the report because it disqualifies the companion results.

claim_judgements.text: DEM discrete lattice cannot reproduce continuum Hertz contact.

evidence.quote: - DEM discrete lattice cannot reproduce continuum Hertz contact

claim_judgements.reasoning: Refuted as stated (a universal/structural claim drawn from one confounded run). The supported version is narrower: 'in this setup (delta/R = 0.5, tool_speed 5 m/s, 4x3x4 assembly, E_dem = k_bond/(2r) calibration) the fitted law deviates from Hertz'. See F3/F4 for the un-excluded causes.

claim_judgements.text: Beam FD shows second-order convergence (error proportional to 1/n^2).
claim_judgements.reasoning: A convergence order requires errors at >=3 resolutions and a fitted slope; the report shows one undefined 'Mesh conv' number and the word 'converging'. Order 2 is plausible for the Euler-Bernoulli FD stencil but is unmeasured here.
No schema file, $id, validator version or exit status; the sentence is not checkable and should stay unresolved in any extraction (F2).

limitations: Single channel: the platform reports list returns at most the newest 50-100 rows and ignores ?tag=/?offset=, so absence of a kf-wp:wp-331-01 record is 'not found on the reachable window', not proof of non-existence; psql on tensor_reports is permission-denied for this identity.

Reviewer sees only report markdown + record metadata; no producer explanation, no prior review events, no code — therefore root-cause statements about the solver (integrator choice, contact model) are inferences from the parameter line, marked as such.

No finding here marks any claim as verified; verification is the platform gate's job.
